clauses.title: Daily Water Withdrawal Cap
clauses.text: Operator shall not withdraw more than 1,205,000 gallons per day from any combination of water sources. Daily withdrawal shall be measured by calibrated meters at all intake points and reported monthly to [Authority].

clauses.title: Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE) Maximum
clauses.text: Facility shall maintain a Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE) ratio not exceeding 1.8 L/kWh, measured quarterly per The Green Grid / ISO 30134 methodology. Failure to meet this target for two consecutive quarters shall trigger a mandatory efficiency improvement plan.

clauses.title: Recycled/Reclaimed Water Requirement
clauses.text: Operator shall source a minimum of 55% of on-site cooling water from recycled, reclaimed, or non-potable sources within 36 months of initial operation. A transition plan with interim milestones shall be submitted to [Authority] within 120 days.

clauses.title: Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) Target
clauses.text: Facility shall achieve and maintain an annualized Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of 1.26 or lower, measured per ISO 30134-2. PUE shall be reported to [Authority] quarterly. If PUE exceeds 1.38 for any two consecutive quarters, Operator shall submit a corrective action plan within 30 days.

clauses.title: Carbon Emission Cap
clauses.text: Annual Scope 1 and Scope 2 carbon emissions shall not exceed 307,133 tonnes CO2e. Operator shall purchase verified carbon offsets or renewable energy certificates for any exceedance within the same calendar year. Emissions shall be reported annually per the Greenhouse Gas Protocol.

clauses.title: Renewable Energy Procurement
clauses.text: Operator shall procure a minimum of 70% of total electricity consumption from certified renewable sources (solar, wind, hydroelectric, or nuclear) within 60 months of initial operation. Interim targets: 55% by Year 1, 60% by Year 3. Verification via renewable energy certificates or direct power purchase agreements.

clauses.title: Generator Emission Standards
clauses.text: All backup generators shall meet or exceed EPA Tier IV emission standards. Maximum combined NOx emissions shall not exceed 7.68 tonnes per year (90% reduction from uncontrolled baseline of 76.80 tonnes). Annual emissions testing by a certified third-party laboratory shall be submitted to [Authority] and the local health department.

clauses.title: Generator Runtime Limitation
clauses.text: Non-emergency generator operation shall not exceed 100 hours per year per unit, consistent with EPA federal requirements. Operator shall maintain runtime logs accessible to [Authority] upon 48-hour notice. Any emergency operation exceeding 24 continuous hours shall be reported to [Authority] within 72 hours.

clauses.title: Community Health Mitigation Fund
clauses.text: Operator shall contribute $100,000 annually to a Community Health Mitigation Fund administered by [Local Health Authority]. Funds shall be directed to respiratory health programs, air quality monitoring equipment, and health screenings within a 10-kilometer radius of the facility.

clauses.title: Noise Limit at Property Boundary
clauses.text: Facility noise shall not exceed 55 dBA (A-weighted, Leq 1-hour) at the nearest residential property boundary between 10:00 PM and 7:00 AM, and 65 dBA during daytime hours, consistent with WHO guidelines. Operator shall install a permanent noise monitoring station at the nearest residential boundary and provide real-time data to [Authority]. Exceedances shall be corrected within 72 hours.

clauses.title: Minimum Permanent Employment
clauses.text: Operator shall create and maintain a minimum of 150 permanent full-time positions at the facility, with an average annual compensation (wages plus benefits) not less than 120% of the county median household income. If employment falls below this threshold for more than 6 months, tax incentive benefits shall be proportionally reduced.

clauses.title: Local Hiring & Apprenticeship
clauses.text: During the construction phase (estimated 1,500 workers), Operator shall ensure that no less than 30% of construction labor hours are performed by workers residing within the county. Operator shall partner with local workforce development agencies to establish apprenticeship programs for at least 50 positions in electrical, HVAC, and IT infrastructure trades.

clauses.title: Tax Incentive Clawback
clauses.text: Tax abatements and incentives (valued at $10.0M/yr) are contingent upon meeting all employment, environmental, and operational commitments in this agreement. Net fiscal capture is currently -38%. If Operator fails to meet any material commitment for 12 consecutive months, [Authority] may recapture up to 100% of incentives provided during the non-compliance period, plus interest at the prime rate.

clauses.title: Community Benefit Fund
clauses.text: Operator shall contribute no less than $1,450,000 annually to a Community Benefit Fund. Fund disbursements shall be governed by a Community Advisory Board with at least 50% membership from residents within 5 miles of the facility. Eligible uses include infrastructure improvements, education, environmental remediation, and public health programs.

clauses.title: Infrastructure Cost Responsibility
clauses.text: Operator shall fund 100% of the following infrastructure improvements required by this development: grid upgrades ($50.0M), road improvements ($8.0M). Total estimated public infrastructure cost: $58.0M. Operator shall post a performance bond equal to 110% of estimated costs prior to construction commencement.

clauses.title: Construction Impact Mitigation
clauses.text: During the estimated 24-month construction period, Operator shall: (a) limit heavy vehicle traffic to designated routes approved by [Authority]; (b) maintain a 24-hour complaint hotline; (c) repair any road damage caused by construction vehicles within 30 days; (d) comply with all local noise ordinances during construction hours.

clauses.title: Stormwater Management
clauses.text: Operator shall implement a stormwater management system that retains or infiltrates the first 25mm of rainfall on-site. Net increase in stormwater runoff shall not exceed 10% of pre-development levels. Estimated annual runoff increase: 566,580 cubic meters (227 Olympic pools). Operator shall submit a stormwater pollution prevention plan (SWPPP) to [Authority] prior to construction.

clauses.title: Carbon Sequestration Offset
clauses.text: Development will eliminate approximately 120.0 tonnes CO2e/yr of carbon sequestration from the converted 200-acre site. Operator shall offset this loss by funding the permanent conservation of at least 300 acres of equivalent or higher-quality habitat within the same watershed, or by purchasing verified carbon credits equivalent to 150% of annual sequestration loss.

clauses.title: Agricultural Mitigation
clauses.text: Conversion of 200 acres eliminates approximately $105k/yr in agricultural revenue. Operator shall fund an Agricultural Preservation Fund of $52,500 annually to support local farmland preservation easements and displaced tenant farmer relocation assistance.

Annual e-waste report shall be submitted to [Authority].

Operator shall submit a stormwater pollution prevention plan (SWPPP) to [Authority] prior to construction.

clauses.title: Carbon Sequestration Offset
clauses.text: Development will eliminate approximately 26.1 tonnes CO2e/yr of carbon sequestration from the converted 522-acre site. Operator shall offset this loss by funding the permanent conservation of at least 783 acres of equivalent or higher-quality habitat within the same watershed, or by purchasing verified carbon credits equivalent to 150% of annual sequestration loss.

clauses.title: Waste Heat Management
clauses.text: Facility generates approximately 75.0 MW of waste heat, of which 45.0 MW is currently rejected to the atmosphere. Operator shall implement a waste heat recovery plan within 48 months that captures a minimum of 30% of waste heat for productive use (district heating, industrial processes, or agricultural applications).

clauses.title: E-Waste & Circular Economy
clauses.text: Operator shall achieve a minimum 80% hardware reuse/recycling rate for all decommissioned equipment, with less than 5% sent to landfill. Operator shall maintain chain-of-custody documentation for all e-waste and shall not export e-waste to countries lacking equivalent environmental standards. Annual e-waste report shall be submitted to [Authority].

clauses.title: Quarterly Impact Report
clauses.text: Operator shall submit a public Quarterly Impact Report to [Authority] containing: (a) PUE and WUE metrics; (b) total electricity and water consumption; (c) generator runtime hours and emissions; (d) employment headcount and payroll; (e) noise monitoring data; (f) any permit exceedances. Reports shall be published on a publicly accessible website within 30 days of quarter-end.

clauses.title: Independent Annual Audit
clauses.text: An independent third-party auditor, selected jointly by [Authority] and Operator, shall conduct an annual compliance audit covering all terms of this Agreement. Audit costs shall be borne by Operator. Audit findings shall be presented to [Authority] and made publicly available within 60 days of completion.

clauses.title: Public Disclosure — No NDAs on Impact Data
clauses.text: No provision of this Agreement, or of any related development agreement, utility contract, or tax incentive, shall restrict the public disclosure of environmental, operational, or fiscal impact data. All impact metrics required by this Agreement are public records.

clauses.title: Penalty for Material Non-Compliance
clauses.text: Material non-compliance with any term of this Agreement, if not cured within 60 days of written notice, shall result in: (a) daily penalties of $10,000 per day per violation; (b) suspension of tax incentives; (c) mandatory public hearing before [Authority]. Three material violations within any 24-month period shall trigger full incentive clawback proceedings.

clauses.title: Agreement Duration & Review
clauses.text: This Agreement shall remain in force for the operational life of the facility, with mandatory review every 5 years. Upon review, either party may propose amendments reflecting changes in technology, regulation, or community needs. Material changes to facility operations (capacity expansion, cooling system change, ownership transfer) require [Authority] approval and may trigger Agreement renegotiation.

clauses.title: Daily Water Withdrawal Cap
clauses.text: Operator shall not withdraw more than 18,000 gallons per day from any combination of water sources. Daily withdrawal shall be measured by calibrated meters at all intake points and reported monthly to [Authority].

clauses.title: Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE) Maximum
clauses.text: Facility shall maintain a Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE) ratio not exceeding 0.1 L/kWh, measured quarterly per The Green Grid / ISO 30134 methodology. Failure to meet this target for two consecutive quarters shall trigger a mandatory efficiency improvement plan.

clauses.title: Recycled/Reclaimed Water Requirement
clauses.text: Operator shall source a minimum of 50% of on-site cooling water from recycled, reclaimed, or non-potable sources within 36 months of initial operation. A transition plan with interim milestones shall be submitted to [Authority] within 120 days.

clauses.title: Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) Target
clauses.text: Facility shall achieve and maintain an annualized Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of 1.14 or lower, measured per ISO 30134-2. PUE shall be reported to [Authority] quarterly. If PUE exceeds 1.25 for any two consecutive quarters, Operator shall submit a corrective action plan within 30 days.

clauses.title: Carbon Emission Cap
clauses.text: Annual Scope 1 and Scope 2 carbon emissions shall not exceed 10,282 tonnes CO2e. Operator shall purchase verified carbon offsets or renewable energy certificates for any exceedance within the same calendar year. Emissions shall be reported annually per the Greenhouse Gas Protocol.

clauses.title: Renewable Energy Procurement
clauses.text: Operator shall procure a minimum of 100% of total electricity consumption from certified renewable sources (solar, wind, hydroelectric, or nuclear) within 60 months of initial operation. Interim targets: 100% by Year 1, 100% by Year 3. Verification via renewable energy certificates or direct power purchase agreements.

clauses.title: Generator Emission Standards
clauses.text: All backup generators shall meet or exceed EPA Tier IV emission standards. Maximum combined NOx emissions shall not exceed 0.04 tonnes per year (90% reduction from uncontrolled baseline of 0.43 tonnes). Annual emissions testing by a certified third-party laboratory shall be submitted to [Authority] and the local health department.

clauses.title: Generator Runtime Limitation
clauses.text: Non-emergency generator operation shall not exceed 100 hours per year per unit, consistent with EPA federal requirements. Operator shall maintain runtime logs accessible to [Authority] upon 48-hour notice. Any emergency operation exceeding 24 continuous hours shall be reported to [Authority] within 72 hours.

clauses.title: Community Health Mitigation Fund
clauses.text: Operator shall contribute $100,000 annually to a Community Health Mitigation Fund administered by [Local Health Authority]. Funds shall be directed to respiratory health programs, air quality monitoring equipment, and health screenings within a 10-kilometer radius of the facility.

clauses.title: Noise Limit at Property Boundary
clauses.text: Facility noise shall not exceed 55 dBA (A-weighted, Leq 1-hour) at the nearest residential property boundary between 10:00 PM and 7:00 AM, and 65 dBA during daytime hours, consistent with WHO guidelines. Operator shall install a permanent noise monitoring station at the nearest residential boundary and provide real-time data to [Authority]. Exceedances shall be corrected within 72 hours.

clauses.title: Minimum Permanent Employment
clauses.text: Operator shall create and maintain a minimum of 300 permanent full-time positions at the facility, with an average annual compensation (wages plus benefits) not less than 120% of the county median household income. If employment falls below this threshold for more than 6 months, tax incentive benefits shall be proportionally reduced.

clauses.title: Local Hiring & Apprenticeship
clauses.text: During the construction phase (estimated 800 workers), Operator shall ensure that no less than 30% of construction labor hours are performed by workers residing within the county. Operator shall partner with local workforce development agencies to establish apprenticeship programs for at least 50 positions in electrical, HVAC, and IT infrastructure trades.

clauses.title: Tax Incentive Clawback
clauses.text: Tax abatements and incentives (valued at $0.0M/yr) are contingent upon meeting all employment, environmental, and operational commitments in this agreement. Net fiscal capture is currently 20%. If Operator fails to meet any material commitment for 12 consecutive months, [Authority] may recapture up to 100% of incentives provided during the non-compliance period, plus interest at the prime rate.

The utility shall file a separate rate class for data center service.
